era_setting.place: Clarence Center and Buffalo, New York, and Newark, New Jersey, USA
era_setting.notes: The night is 12 February 2009. The film runs forward to the NTSB report of February 2010 and the Act of August 2010. Late-2000s American regional aviation: Q400 turboprops, CRT-era airline crew rooms, 2009 cars and phones. Nothing from the 2020s may appear as present-day.

forbidden_claims: That fatigue caused the crash. The Board concluded the pilots' performance was likely impaired by fatigue but that the extent and the degree of contribution could not be conclusively determined (FACTS_LEDGER row CO-801).

That the captain lied on his employment application. The record says his answer was incomplete, and that Colgan stated a complete answer would have ended his employment (FACTS_LEDGER rows CO-502, CO-503, CO-504).
That the first officer's pay or her overnight commute caused the accident. Neither appears in the probable cause or in any of the four contributing factors (FACTS_LEDGER rows CO-201, CO-202).
That the 1,500-hour rule would have prevented this crash. The captain held an airline transport pilot certificate; the rule addresses first officers (FACTS_LEDGER rows CO-404, CO-902).
That the crew were unqualified. Both held current certificates and met the requirements in force at the time (FACTS_LEDGER rows CO-601, CO-604).
Any characterisation of either pilot's state of mind, feelings or home life beyond what the record states. Both died in this accident and cannot answer.
Any detail of the deaths, the fire, or the people in the house on the ground.
That the pilot records database exists because of this crash, stated as fact, until Public Law 111-216 has been opened and read (FACTS_LEDGER row CO-904).

beats.headline: FIVE MILES SHORT
beats.notes: Five nautical miles north-east of the runway. The map stops there. No crash site.

beats.headline: WHAT THE RED BAR IS FOR
beats.notes: The low-speed cue rising up the airspeed scale, the numbers turning from white to red.

beats.headline: WINGS LEVEL, ONE G
beats.notes: The Board's own finding that there was enough airspeed available to correct it.

beats.headline: PUSH / PULL
beats.notes: The stick pusher is an instruction. Two arrows, one right, one wrong. No blame on the card.
Four disapprovals across sixteen years, built one at a time.

beats.headline: ONE LINE ON A FORM
beats.notes: The application question. Illustrate a form; no legible text is generated.

beats.headline: WHAT WAS ASKED / WHAT WAS ANSWERED
THIRTEEN POINT ONE PER CENT
beats.notes: The 2008 ATP first-attempt failure rate. This card exists so the film cannot imply that failing is rare.

beats.headline: WHAT EACH SEAT EARNED
beats.source: FACTS_LEDGER rows CO-605, CO-606 and CO-701

beats.headline: COULD NOT BE CONCLUSIVELY DETERMINED
beats.notes: The Board's sentence about fatigue, on screen, in its own words. The restraint is the point.

notes: EP78 replaced Fukushima on 2026-08-24 after that premise died (the Tokyo High Court overturned the 13 trillion yen order on 6 June 2025). Runtime and word bands follow the owner's 2026-08-23 decision for the slate: 29-32 minutes, divided at the measured 160 wpm, never 176. The source is NTSB/AAR-10/01, fetched and read at 299 pages. Two people in this file died in the accident and the Board's probable cause names one of them; forbidden_claims exists mostly to stop this film becoming an accusation against a dead pilot when the Board found four contributing factors and only one of them is a person in a seat.
